title: Clean up POSIX verification subprocesses on SIGTERM
body:
SIGTERM sent to either POSIX verification owner can terminate the owner while its separately grouped module and solver keep running. A readiness-controlled baseline fixture observes both descendants still alive after owner exit `-15`. Existing timeout and KeyboardInterrupt cleanup do not run for default SIGTERM.

This change temporarily handles default SIGTERM during main-thread calls to `research_package.run_command` and `run_isolated_tests.run_modules`, then uses their existing process-group cleanup. A normal handled termination exits 143, restores the previous handler and never reports verification success. The registered path covers Python replay and optional dependency-install commands; the isolated path retains result order and queued-work cancellation. Custom/ignored handlers, worker-thread invocation and Windows ownership retain their existing behavior.

Launch/assignment and cleanup only record pending termination. Asynchronous cancellation is permitted only inside a wait protected by an inner `finally`. A signal before Popen returns therefore cannot lose its spawned handle; the isolated workers retain the existing launch/registration lock. Repeated SIGTERM cannot interrupt cleanup. If an ordinary exception has already entered cleanup, the first SIGTERM is deferred and the original exception remains the failure. This closes a distinct cancellation boundary beyond #2625/#2676, #2906, #4683 and #4779. Detached sessions and SIGKILL remain outside scope.

Validation on macOS 27 arm64 / CPython 3.12.2:

- Eleven new methods / twenty real-process fixtures pass normally and with the actual owner interpreter optimized (13.742 s / 13.660 s). Native kqueue exit observations precede independent fixture teardown. Coverage includes both entry points, launch races, queue cancellation, repeated signals, ordinary completion and exceptional cleanup, handler preservation/restoration, and worker-thread calls.
- The exception-cleanup fixture holds two isolated process groups/four observed processes, injects an ordinary failure, then sends the first SIGTERM from the first cleanup call. Every group exits and the original failure survives. A parent-only cleanup mutation is rejected for both owners.
- Five existing focused unittest groups: 71 passes / 30 platform skips (101 total). Optimized isolated/registered-bytecode/onboarding compatibility: 61 passes / 23 skips (84 total).
- Complete unchanged `isolated-test-bytecode` and `isolated-descendant-bytecode` registered hooks pass in 7.995 s / 24.085 s. The standalone copied-runner boundary remains supported; no new helper import is required.
- `git diff --check` passes. Three meaningful commits retain the regression, root repair and scope/evidence note; every author and committer is JoyboyBrian.

The new `test_research_posix_sigterm.py` is included by existing Ubuntu onboarding CI. At exact head `7cffe39596aae05003391f22a4a9c452501b27ae`, [Ubuntu onboarding job120251366422](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39903905293/job/120251366422) passed on Ubuntu 24.04.5 / CPython 3.12.15: all eleven new SIGTERM methods passed with native pidfd lifetime observations, and the complete onboarding suite passed 373 tests with eleven platform skips. The downstream full archive CI remains unverified. Changing shared `scripts/research_package.py` makes the actual planner select all **2,851 opted-in packages** at this base; those historical/scientific packages were not replayed locally. The separately inspected `isolated-runner-successor` metadata still rejects its unchanged historical `certificates/selected-result.json` pin before replay. No frozen pin, acceptance list, selected record or mathematical claim is changed, and full archive CI is not claimed green.

Base: canonical `b91956876e5b4122fd89179f1b57557ff8378f15`, priority revision 7. Exact commands, source hashes, signal/exit-status contract and open obligations are in `docs/research/posix-sigterm-cleanup.md`. [Canonical claim and investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1472#discussioncomment-19138316).

The eight metadata failures reproduce with the original base `scripts/research_package.py`, base package metadata and base source bytes, using `--check-only`. For `adaptive-witness-retune`, `a5-conjugate-any-registers` and `bidirectional-connector`, `--check-only` passes at both revisions; their own unchanged verifier/caller separately treats historical selected-result provenance as a live hash. Executing only those exact source-authentication guards from the base reproduces their logged exceptions. Their scientific routines were not rerun locally. All eleven relevant verifier/caller and metadata files, and both mismatched source targets, are byte-identical between base and this PR. These eleven inspected causes therefore predate this change; pending or subsequently completed archive jobs have not been triaged. No full archive success or baseline scientific replay is claimed. Frozen pins remain unchanged.
